name: Glass graph
what: A glass stat card under your chin: it rises into place, a line graph climbs across it with a glowing head and a soft fill while the big number counts up (0 to 197K, 82 %, $4,900...); the number pops as it lands, the head sends out a ring every second, a band of light crosses the glass, and it sinks away at the end.
origin: Rebuilt after the liquid-glass-graph effect of claude-video-effects (MIT): a glass card with a climbing graph and a number counting up - MotionLab's own code, a glass card made part of the shot
motion: f0-f12 the card rises 86 px and grows from 88 % (slow end, seen within 4 f) while its 3 grid lines draw in (12 f each, 3 f apart); f8-f68 the line climbs across (climb = 60 f, S-curve) with a glowing head and a fill under it, the number counting with the same curve; f68 the number pops (7 %, 8 f, slow end) and the head swells; from then a ring leaves the head every 30 f (14 f, slow end) and the card floats 3 px; a band of light crosses the glass f72-f96 (S-curve); the last 9 f it sinks 30 px and fades (accelerating)
